## STRUCTURE MUST KEEP
Edit input1 into ONE finished concept image, retaining this daytime city diorama, the same two buildings, road bend, parked gray sedan, two open rear exits and full square cutaway base. Preserve architecture except the explicitly smaller ground floor of the four-storey building below. Repaint the surface rendering substantially: preservation of layout does NOT mean preservation of smooth rendering. Use one ORTHOGRAPHIC PARALLEL camera, shared XYZ scale. Level straight edges of base, paving, foundations, floor bands, walls and roofs in a common world direction must remain parallel across all heights and depths. Keep complete framing, sharp square planar base, exactly two visible front planar cuts, corresponding vertical corners with equal extrusion depth. Reconstruct inconsistent base thickness or projection rather than preserving source errors. No perspective convergence, twisted floor, rounded/beveled base or arbitrary building rotation. Rounded corners of building B remain allowed; curve tangents and diagonal support braces are not XY horizontal lines.

Exactly two open street transitions: one rear-left beside A, one rear-right beside B. Retain continuous high boundary walls elsewhere. Clear central street bend and both approach/turn/transition volumes; put additions along edges without blocking access or hiding ground connections. Building doors are ordinary entrances, not extra map exits. Retain credible grounded human entrances and upper-floor access cores. Keep each building's roof roughly40–80% purposefully occupied by the existing service equipment/decks with visible supports and remaining roof area; do not multiply equipment. Four floors on A/two floors on B remain the user's scene-specific height exception, not new global limits. Input2 is only the revised structural illustration, no diagram labels or colors in final.

## CURRENT SCENE
Make ALL the following visible changes to input1:

1. PAINTED SURFACE EXPRESSION: The current smooth render is specifically rejected for lacking readable brushwork. On intact wall panels, machine housings, asphalt and vehicle panels, use clearly visible BROAD FLAT DIRECTIONAL PAINT STROKES and simplified adjoining color planes like input5. Some long strokes follow wall height or panel direction, with grouped angular strokes on ground. Use close but distinguishable hue/value changes, large deliberate stroke shapes and calm base-color gaps. The stroke character must read at normal full-image viewing size, not only microscopic zoom. Repaint smooth gradients into designed planar color transitions while keeping coherent 3D shading and materials. These strokes must also appear on UNDAMAGED painted surfaces. They are NOT peeling paint, grime, cracks or random speckles. Do not solve this request by adding dirt. No raised impasto, all-over crosshatch/noise, wavy glass, tiny mosaic brush marks, blurred edges or photographic miniature microtexture.

2. REMOVE ALL NEON: physically delete every cyan/magenta glowing strip and its housing from A/B. No neon signs, colored emissive panels or substitute glowing bars. Retain ordinary non-neon fixtures if appropriate to daylight. Remain DAYTIME with DRY pavement, natural sunlight and cool sky fill, no wet reflections or puddles.

3. WALL DESIGN: break up the uniform pale wall color with a few selected large painted graphic areas and faded hand-painted graffiti. Use a muted brick-red abstract interlocking emblem on one exposed A wall, and a broad desaturated blue-green broken band/geometric motif on another building or boundary wall. Include visibly brushed edges and repaired sections. Keep them as intentional wall graphics with surrounding quiet color planes, not repeated wallpaper across every wall or random dirt. No legible slogans, logos, UI, floor labels or arrows required. Graffiti/pattern design is ADDITIONAL to the brush-painted surface rendering, not its substitute.

4. FOUR-STOREY BUILDING A at left/back: make the FIRST/GROUND FLOOR visibly SMALLER IN FOOTPRINT than the SECOND FLOOR. Recess first-floor front and side walls by approximately one doorway width where feasible, retaining human entrance and structural access core; second floor stays its existing larger size and projects beyond the smaller ground enclosure. Show coherent load-bearing piers and transfer beams under this wider second floor, outside walking routes. Four floors total: SMALL OCCUPIED GROUND FLOOR / LARGER OCCUPIED SECOND FLOOR / existing NONRESIDENTIAL MACHINERY THIRD FLOOR / existing LARGER OCCUPIED FOURTH FLOOR. Retain the third-floor equipment volume and its larger supported fourth-floor cap. Do not shrink second floor or hide the ground-floor size change with a new bulky facade. All setbacks translate along shared X/Y, no diagonal rotation.

5. RIGHT BUILDING B: preserve its whole first-floor machinery volume, larger slightly offset rounded-corner second-floor habitation, clear brackets/columns and existing rooftop heat exchanger. Change its surface expression, selected wall graphics and neon removal as above; do not revert it to an ordinary two-storey box.

6. ROAD / SMALL PROPS: keep the dry road usable but less pristine. Add a small number of localized SHALLOW BROKEN ASPHALT PATCHES with a few broad cracks and exposed coarse chunks near curb sections, plus a few loose cream/gray PAPER LITTER SHEETS gathered along road edges. Keep central combat floor and exit approaches mostly clear. No continuous canyon-like crack, collapsed road, litter blanket, bags or garbage piles. Add ONE readable old red FIRE HYDRANT with side caps and a few repair marks, grounded on the building-side sidewalk near the foreground, clear of doors and vehicle route.

7. BUILDING-SIDE PAVEMENT: add a LARGE-SCALE geometric TILE INLAY PATTERN in muted charcoal, warm cream and restrained terracotta. Use broad stepped-square bands or grouped large squares running on the same X/Y paving grid; distinct at full-image scale. Keep it FLAT and supported by the existing sidewalk, with subtle selected chips and painted tonal strokes. No tiny busy mosaics, perspective-warping optical illusion or large physical height changes. Keep the road separate from patterned pedestrian pavement.

Retain the two buildings' identities, one car, overall urban drainage/power cutaway, current machinery proportions and dry daylight. The small asphalt damage and litter do not imply a ruined or flooded city. Changes apply to this edit only.

## ART / REFERENCE ROLES
Maintain Little Devil Inside's simplified readable architecture, differentiated materials, large light/shadow shapes and organized density, with the master-approved BROAD FLAT BRUSHWORK made clearly visible through input5. Maintain Salvage Cyberpunk: reused advanced machinery, repaired painted casings, thick purposeful joints/conduits and old buildings kept functioning. Broad color strokes, designed wall graphics, material wear and actual geometry are four distinct things; don't replace all four with grime. Avoid uniform plastic rendering, tiny photoreal detailing, overly sharp equal scratches, or a featureless solid-color fill.

INPUT1 is the user-selected edit target, only identity/layout and retained architecture; its smooth finish and uncertain geometry are NOT approved references. INPUT2 is the current structural guide for the smaller A ground floor, unchanged equipment floors, square base and two-exit connectivity, derived from Master01/02. INPUT3 M03-10 supplies LDI architecture/material/light readability only, NOT its camera, world, shops, people or UI. INPUT4 M04-02 supplies heavy salvaged mechanical housing/joint design only, NOT its person/exoskeleton or photographic texture. INPUT5 B03-01 supplies ONLY the broad, deliberate, flat painted surface strokes/color planes on intact areas. Do NOT copy input5's architecture, perspective, fantasy overhang, waterfront, time/palette, boat, people, signs or layout. Common orthographic camera overrides every source camera. The added wall graffiti and tile motif are requested in-world graphics; no annotation overlays or collages. Deliver ONE full diorama image.
